JUDGEMENT CALLS (all five deg-4 rail/column crossings on the middle rail)
  The drafter dots junctions habitually on this sheet: S2 (291,312), S3 (517,314), S4 (728,317) are deg-3 Ts that did NOT need a dot and got one anyway. So a bare deg-4 X here is meaningful evidence of a crossing, which is the brief's rule 3 overriding the generic ink prior. Pixel dumps (inkmap, stroke width ~2-3 px):
  * S22 (289,472) -> JUNCTION. Solder blob spans rows 469-477 x cols 285-292, i.e. ~8x9 px = ~3x stroke width in both axes. A real dot. Crossing instead would have split the 290 column (Zener #2 bottom + Diode #14 top) off the ground rail, leaving GND touching only the 9uF plate.
  * S26 (726,477) -> JUNCTION. Same signature: vertical widens from 3 px to 9 px over rows 472-479. A real dot. Crossing instead would have made {Zener #6 bottom, Diode #10 top} a private 2-terminal net and left the 9uF right plate wired only to the 4uH.
  * S23 (518,471) -> CROSSING (override of the tracer default). No blob: the vertical stays 2-3 px and only reaches 5 px where the 3-px rail overlaps it - about 2x, versus the ~3x of the real dots 200 px either side. The junction reading would have merged Diode #4 bottom and Zener #11 top into n7, giving one 6-terminal middle-rail net and deleting n5.
  * S24 (91,474) -> CROSSING (override). Cleanest case: the inkmap shows a constant 3-px vertical and a constant 3-px horizontal with zero thickening at the meeting point. The junction reading would have tied V-AC #3 bottom and I-DC #13 top to ground, deleting n4; both readings are electrically sane (as a crossing the left column is the series chain L#1 - V-AC#3 - I-DC#13 - C#17 between the top and bottom rails), so the ink decided it.
  * S27 (927,477) -> CROSSING (override). No blob; the vertical is 2-3 px through the intersection with only a 4-px smear below. Junction would have merged n6 (Diode #5 bottom / Diode #12 top) with n8 (4uH right end / Resistor #15 top) into one 4-terminal net. Both readings sane, so again the bare ink decided it. Note the tracer's own dot score agreed with S26 (1.8 = 1.8), which is why this needed the pixel dump rather than the score.
  All deg-3 sites on the top and bottom rails (S2, S3, S4, S43, S44, S45) are unambiguous Ts - a wire terminating on a rail - and are recorded as junctions. Every other listed site is ink from a handwritten value label or from a component symbol and changes nothing.

WHY THE FIRST PASS'S RULE-3 ARGUMENT DOES NOT HOLD. It rested on the premise
that "the drafter dots junctions habitually on this sheet", evidenced by the
three top-rail Ts S2/S3/S4 that were dotted although a T needs no dot. That
premise is only half true, and the other half reverses the conclusion. Pixel
dumps of the three BOTTOM-rail Ts show no dot at all:
  S45 (285,652): vertical is 3 px (x=285..287) right down to the rail, rail is
    3-4 px (y=651..654); no thickening at the meeting point.
  S44 (513,648): vertical 4 px (x=512..515), rail 3-4 px (y=647..651); no blob.
  S43 (731,641): vertical 3-4 px (x=730..733), rail 3-4 px (y=641..644); no blob.
  Contrast the genuinely dotted top-rail Ts: S2 (291,312) blob ~6x8 px over
  rows 307-314, S3 (517,314) blob ~8x8 over rows 310-317, S4 (728,317) ~5x8.
So this drafter dotted the top rail and stopped bothering on the bottom rail.
A bare intersection on this sheet therefore carries no information: absence of
a dot is the drafter's default, not a statement of "no connection".

WHAT THE INK DOES SAY. There is not one hop, jog or semicircle anywhere on this
sheet - the drafter's hop metric is 0.0 at every site except the noise-level
2.1/3.6 that is just hand wobble in the rail's y (checked in the dumps: at
(91,474) the rail runs y=473-475 on the left and y=473-474 on the right, at
(518,471) and (927,477) it is flat through the crossing). In this dataset the
drafters draw a hop or a jog when they mean "not connected" (brief, rule 2), so
a sheet with zero hops is a sheet with zero intended crossings. All five deg-4
middle-rail intersections are junctions.

SIBLING / STRUCTURE EVIDENCE (decisive). circuit_1124 is the SAME generated
circuit drawn by a different hand in the same 3-rail x 5-column layout with the
same values (8V/1kHz V-AC, 3A I-DC, 5uH, 15uF, 9uF, 4uH, 1uF, three 5V zeners,
2k resistor, two GNDs). It is human-verified at 9 nets, and in that drawing the
middle rail carries NO dots at all yet every one of its five column crossings is
annotated as a junction - e.g. its V-AC bottom and I-DC top both sit on '0' with
the two GNDs. Running a labelled-graph isomorphism test, the 9-net reading above
is isomorphic to all eight of the 9-net verified siblings (1122, 1124, 155, 303,
324, 678, 750, 755); the previous 12-net reading is isomorphic to none of the
ten siblings. The nine resulting nets also match the siblings' node signature
term for term:
  0   (8) Cap#7, Diode#14, GND#8, GND#18, I-DC#13, Resistor#15, V-AC#3, Zener#2
  n1  (4) Cap#0, Diode#4, Inductor#1, Zener#2
  n2  (3) Cap#0, Diode#5, Zener#6
  n3  (2) Inductor#1, V-AC#3
  n4  (6) Cap#7, Diode#4, Diode#10, Inductor#9, Zener#6, Zener#11
  n5  (4) Diode#5, Diode#12, Inductor#9, Resistor#15
  n6  (3) Diode#10, Diode#12, Inductor#16
  n7  (4) Cap#17, Diode#14, Inductor#16, Zener#11
  n8  (2) Cap#17, I-DC#13
Physically this is the natural reading of the drawing: every one of the five
columns carries a part above the middle rail and a part below it, so the middle
rail node is a real node of each column - that is the whole point of the
3-rail ladder. The old reading instead made three of the five columns pass
straight through the middle rail, which would have left the rail crossing them
for no reason.
